## Overview

The UK Government’s Green Book sets out how to appraise costs, benefits and risks to achieve public sector objectives. It recommends the Five Case Model as the standard framework for developing robust business cases for projects and programmes. APMG International’s Better Business Cases qualification is based on the ‘Five Case Model’ methodology – a best-practice approach originally developed for the public sector to guide strategic planning and investment decisions at the government level.

Better Business Cases certification helps professionals build strong, value-driven proposals that win support and funding.

The digital content will take approximately 18 hours to complete (although some learners may wish to spend longer to help prepare more effectively) and there is additional UK Government Guidance to support your study. Note: there is no exam voucher included in this product. If you do wish to purchase this course with the exam you can do so here. Alternatively, you may purchase the exam at a later date. However, if you do so we recommend not leaving it too long after completing the course and you ideally sit the exam within a 4-week period to maintain focus and ensure suitable knowledge is retained.

## Prerequisites

There are no formal pre-requisites for Better Business Cases Foundation.

### Target Audience

Better Business Cases certification is aimed at professionals who play a key role in creating, delivering, or reporting the value of investments, and is suitable for anyone who:

- Wants to deepen their understanding of Better Business Cases processes and techniques.
- Is responsible for the successful delivery of programmes and projects, such as Senior Responsible Owners (SROs) or Programme Directors.
- Is responsible for developing a business case for investment, such as Project Managers, Project Team members and other specialist advisors.
- Is involved in the scrutiny and review of investment proposals.

## Outline

Throughout this course, you will learn to work effectively with a team to develop a strong business case. The content is covered in detail within the following lessons.

Introduction to Better Business Cases

This lesson will cover the purpose, value and benefits of Better Business Cases and explain why robust business cases are fundamental to successful programmes and projects. Learners will understand the causes of project failure, the role of business cases in supporting decision-making, and the relationship between projects, programmes and organisational strategy.

Programmes, Projects and the Business Case

This lesson will cover the characteristics of programmes and projects, their relationship to organisational strategy, and the governance arrangements that support successful investment decisions. Learners will understand programme and project assurance, business case ownership, and how Better Business Cases aligns with recognised project and programme management methodologies.

Overview of the Five Case Model

This lesson will cover the principles of the Five Case Model and its role within business case development. Learners will understand the purpose of the Strategic, Economic, Commercial, Financial and Management Cases and how each contributes to robust investment decision-making.

Business Case Development Process and Types of Business Case

This lesson will cover the stages of business case development and the different business case products used throughout the investment lifecycle. Learners will understand the purpose of the Strategic Outline Case, Outline Business Case, Full Business Case and Business Justification Case, alongside the ten-step business case development process.

Determining the Strategic Context

This lesson will cover the activities required to establish strategic fit and confirm the organisational context for an investment proposal. Learners will understand strategic assessment, organisational objectives, governance considerations and the relationship between programmes, projects and strategic portfolios.

Scoping the Proposal – The Strategic Case and Preferred Way Forward

This lesson will cover how to establish the case for change and identify a preferred way forward. Learners will understand spending objectives, business needs, scope, benefits, risks, constraints, dependencies, critical success factors, and the process used to identify and evaluate long-list options.

Planning the Scheme – Determining Value for Money

This lesson will cover how value for money is assessed through appraisal of short-listed options. Learners will understand economic appraisal, costs and benefits, optimism bias, benefits appraisal, risk appraisal, sensitivity analysis and the selection of a preferred option.

Planning the Scheme – Commercial and Financial Cases

This lesson will cover the commercial and financial considerations associated with investment proposals. Learners will understand procurement strategies, risk apportionment, payment mechanisms, affordability, funding requirements and the financial assessments required to support business case approval.

Planning for Successful Delivery – The Management Case

This lesson will cover the arrangements required to support successful project and programme delivery. Learners will understand project management, change management, benefits realisation, risk management, assurance and post-project evaluation arrangements used within the Management Case.

Procuring the Proposal, Reviewing the Business Case and Exam Preparation

This lesson will cover the final stages of the business case lifecycle, including procurement activities, contract arrangements and business case review. Learners will consolidate their understanding of the Five Case Model, business case development process and Foundation examination requirements through revision and exam-focused activities.

### Exams and Assessments

Please not that this eLearning course option does not include the Better Business Cases Foundation exam. If you do wish to purchase this course with the exam you can do so here. Should learners wish to progress and purchase / take the Foundation exam it consists of:

- 50 multiple-choice questions.
- 40 minutes to complete the exam.
- 25 marks are required to pass (25/50) — 50%.

This is a closed-book exam.

Full details of how to take an online APMG exam can be found on its website: Help & Support | APMG International

### What’s Included

- 12 months access to self-paced digital content (estimated 18 hours)
- Sample examination paper

You will be directed to download personal copies of the UK Government’s ‘Guide to Developing the Programme Business Case’ and the ‘Guide to Developing the Project Business Case’.

This content has been developed by QA with the use of APMG International’s Better Business Cases Certification with permission of the APM Group Ltd.

## Learning outcomes

Key things that you will learn on this course include:

- The philosophy and underlying rationale of the Five Case Model methodology.
- The different types of business case, their purpose, who is responsible for them, and when they are required in the development of a spending proposal.
- The development of the business case in relation to other recognized and recommended best practice for programme and project management.

## Frequently asked questions

### How can I create an account on myQA.com?

There are a number of ways to create an account. If you are a self-funder, simply select the "Create account" option on the login page.

If you have been booked onto a course by your company, you will receive a confirmation email. From this email, select "Sign into myQA" and you will be taken to the "Create account" page. Complete all of the details and select "Create account".

If you have the booking number you can also go here and select the "I have a booking number" option. Enter the booking reference and your surname. If the details match, you will be taken to the "Create account" page from where you can enter your details and confirm your account.

Find more answers to frequently asked questions in our FAQs: Bookings & Cancellations page.

### How do QA’s virtual classroom courses work?

Our virtual classroom courses allow you to access award-winning classroom training, without leaving your home or office. Our learning professionals are specially trained on how to interact with remote attendees and our remote labs ensure all participants can take part in hands-on exercises wherever they are.

We use the WebEx video conferencing platform by Cisco. Before you book, check that you meet the WebEx system requirements and run a test meeting to ensure the software is compatible with your firewall settings. If it doesn’t work, try adjusting your settings or contact your IT department about permitting the website.

### How do QA’s online courses work?

QA online courses, also commonly known as distance learning courses or elearning courses, take the form of interactive software designed for individual learning, but you will also have access to full support from our subject-matter experts for the duration of your course.

Once you have purchased the Online course and have completed your registration, you will receive the necessary details to enable you to immediately access it through our e-learning platform and you can start to learn straight away, from any compatible device. Access to the online learning platform is valid for one year from the booking date.

All courses are built around case studies and presented in an engaging format, which includes storytelling elements, video, audio and humour. Every case study is supported by sample documents and a collection of Knowledge Nuggets that provide more in-depth detail on the wider processes.

### When will I receive my joining instructions?

Joining instructions for QA courses are sent two weeks prior to the course start date, or immediately if the booking is confirmed within this timeframe. # Autonomous vessel facility to power future maritime skills

24 November 2026

Southampton Solent University is set to expand its globally renowned maritime teaching and learning portfolio with a new facility dedicated to maritime autonomy, helping to develop the next generation of talent in one of the sector's fastest-growing areas.

Following a successful bid for capital funding from the Office for Students, Solent will launch an ambitious project to establish a dedicated Uncrewed Surface Vessel (USV) learning facility in Southampton.

The facility will provide students with first-hand experience of the technologies transforming the maritime industry, including autonomous vessels, advanced sonar systems, robotics and high-performance computing. Designed to support the growing use of USVs in areas such as hydrographic surveying, environmental monitoring and port security, the project will equip graduates with the practical skills increasingly sought by employers across the maritime sector.

Integrated across a range of existing courses in maritime, engineering and computing disciplines, the new facility will create a unique multidisciplinary learning environment where students can design, programme, operate and maintain autonomous systems. They will also gain experience of managing complex autonomous operations, including how multiple vessels can interact safely and effectively to complete a range of tasks.

The investment reflects the increasing importance of maritime autonomy both regionally and nationally, with industry demand continuing to grow for professionals who can develop, manage and operate autonomous technologies.

Jonathan Ridley, Associate Pro Vice-Chancellor at Southampton Solent University, said:

"USV technology is advancing rapidly, creating exciting opportunities across the maritime sector. There is a clear demand across the region for people with the right skills and knowledge to support this growth.

"This project will ensure our graduates from a range of subject areas can apply their specialist expertise in the context of maritime autonomy and are well prepared for the careers of the future."

The new facility will build on Solent's extensive maritime infrastructure, which already includes the University's 60-metre towing tank, Maritime Simulation Centre, specialist maritime laboratories and Ship Handling Centre at Timsbury Lake.

By combining these established facilities with new autonomous technologies, Solent is further strengthening its position as a leading provider of maritime education, training and applied research. Graduates will leave with the career-ready expertise needed to help drive the future of autonomous maritime technology and support the UK's ambition to remain a global leader in maritime innovation.

The new USV learning facility complements the University's wider investment in maritime innovation through the Solent Maritime Autonomy, Research and Training (SMART) Centre, which opened in January 2026.

Based at Solent's East Park Terrace campus, the SMART Centre brings together education, research and industry engagement to accelerate the development and adoption of maritime autonomous technologies. The centre provides a collaborative environment where students, researchers and industry partners can work together on real-world challenges, helping to advance innovation in autonomous vessels, robotics, artificial intelligence and marine data systems.

Through specialist facilities, applied research projects and close collaboration with industry, the SMART Centre supports regional and national priorities for maritime growth while helping to ensure the UK remains at the forefront of autonomous maritime capability. The centre also creates new opportunities for students to gain industry-relevant experience and develop the advanced technical skills needed to succeed in a rapidly evolving maritime sector.
